A Coup of Tea by Casey Blair – Review

By Julia Kitvaria Sarene August 26, 2026 #A Coup of Tea, #Casey Blair, #cosy fantasy/cozy fantasy, #self-publishing/indie, #Tea Princess Chronicles, #women in sff
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:03
Instaread

When the fourth princess of Istalam is due to dedicate herself to a path serving the crown, she makes a choice that shocks everyone, herself most of all: She leaves.

In hiding and exiled from power, Miyara finds her place running a tea shop in a struggling community that sits on the edge of a magical disaster zone. But there’s more brewing under the surface of this city—hidden magic, and hidden machinations—that threaten all the people who’ve helped her make her own way.

Miyara may not be a princess anymore, but with a teapot in hand she’ll risk her newfound freedom to discover a more meaningful kind of power.

When I picked up A Coup of Tea by Casey Blair, I was ready for a cozy fantasy, and cozy it absolutely delivers. Princess Miyara walks away from her royal life without much of a plan, and ends up finding her footing in a tea shop almost by accident. Her royal background turns out to be more useful than expected, bringing knowledge of tea, treaties, and law to a role that is as much about people as it is about leaves. Watching her build something small and meaningful from that is genuinely charming. No chosen one prophecy, no world ending stakes, just someone trying to figure out where she belongs.

The supporting cast is where the book really shines, and honestly they are more of a hook than the princess herself. The sassy best friend and assassin bodyguard are more compelling than Miyara at almost every turn. Especially the banter and back and forth kept me entertained.

The setting has lovely cozy visuals throughout, and the pacing keeps things light even when the story touches on weightier themes like systemic oppression and immigrant perspectives. That balance is mostly handled well. Less successful about these topics is the worldbuilding, which draws heavily on Asian-inspired tea culture and ceremony without ever quite feeling like an Asian world, a disconnect that is hard to ignore.

The book’s biggest weakness is in how it handles its own stakes. There are real conflicts set up here, ones with weight and consequence, but they tend to resolve quickly and cleanly, leaving little room to breathe or to feel the impact. The pattern repeats often enough that it becomes noticeable: problem appears, problem dissolves, move on. It is not that things should not work out, but fewer higher-stakes moments given more page time to resolve would have served the story better.

Miyara, and how easily things fall into place for her, can be eye-roll inducing, and her privilege follows her out of the palace in ways the story acknowledges but never really interrogates. Though to the book’s credit she is also genuinely caring, willing to apologize, and puts in real effort when it counts.

A Coup of Tea is the literary equivalent of wrapping your hands around a warm mug on a rainy afternoon. Flawed, a little too convenient, but genuinely comforting and exactly what it sets out to be.

By Julia Kitvaria Sarene

Julia Kitvaria Sarene, a Munich native with an unmistakable love for all things fantasy, spent a solid 21 years working as a bookseller. During that time, she became a veritable wizard of book recommendations, guiding countless customers to their next literary adventure. In fact, if you ever walked into a bookshop and heard a voice telling you, “You’ll love this one,” you were probably in her domain. Her heart beats for fantasy novels, but don’t try to talk her into romance. She’s far too busy exploring epic worlds where dragons are more common than love triangles. As a reviewer for Fantasy Faction, Julia brings her enthusiasm and humor to older books as well as the latest fantasy releases, trying to help readers navigate the realm of swords, magic, and supernatural wonders. When she’s not nose-deep in a book or battling the occasional villainous creature on paper, Julia can be found out in the wilds, either running, hiking, or practicing traditional archery. Yes, she’s one of those rare individuals who can probably lose an arrow while discussing the latest fantasy tome. (Loose as in go looking for it, rather than shoot, as she has much more love than talent for archery.) Her adventure doesn’t stop there, she’s also a proud owner of a cute black rescue dog who’s probably the only one who truly understands the complexities of her ever-growing book collection. And if you think her book obsession is a problem, think again. Julia’s collection has reached legendary proportions. She buys more books than any one person can read in a lifetime. No such thing as “too many” books in her world. Since her eyesight is on the decline (a tragic side effect of loving books a little too much), she’s a devoted fan of audiobooks, embracing the power of storytelling in every possible format. So, whether she’s running through forests, reviewing fantasy novels, or playing with Galli, Julia is living proof that life is too short to not enjoy a good adventure, be it in the real world or between the pages of a fantastical story.
